io.credit: NASA / JPL / USGS Astrogeology, Voyager 1 and Galileo SSI
io.artist: NASA / JPL / USGS Astrogeology, Voyager 1 and Galileo SSI
io.usage: A focused polar-projected repair replaces the remaining southern smear and stretched rows with sulfur plains, scalloped lava-flow margins and occasional volcanic depressions. Keeps the large Galileo SSI and Voyager mosaic colors and retains the preceding source tone matching across the two tile edges. Parts of Io were never photographed or were photographed only at low resolution. Those areas are painted with an image model to continue the photographed ground. The painted details are unobserved.

europa.credit: NASA / JPL / U.S. Geological Survey Astrogeology, Voyager and Galileo SSI
europa.artist: NASA / JPL / U.S. Geological Survey Astrogeology, Voyager and Galileo SSI
europa.usage: The USGS 500 m Voyager and Galileo mosaic supplies the measured ice and the sharp fractures. Missing regions and the soft patches are painted to continue that ground. Parts of Europa were never photographed or were photographed only at low resolution. Those areas are painted with an image model to continue the photographed ground. The painted details are unobserved.

ganymede.credit: NASA / JPL / USGS Astrogeology, Voyager 1 and 2 and Galileo SSI
ganymede.artist: NASA / JPL / USGS Astrogeology, Voyager 1 and 2 and Galileo SSI
ganymede.usage: The monochrome mosaic supplies measured relief, and the colour mosaic (https://planetarymaps.usgs.gov/mosaic/Ganymede_Voyager_GalileoSSI_Global_ClrMosaic_1435m.tif, public domain) supplies low-pass colour. Soft or missing ground was painted in equal-area polar views, including the noisy southern Voyager swath. The delivery width is matched to the resolved terrain, and the higher-pixel-count working map is retained. Parts of Ganymede were never photographed or were photographed only at low resolution. Those areas are painted with an image model to continue the photographed ground. The painted details are unobserved.

callisto.credit: NASA / JPL / USGS Astrogeology, Voyager 1 and 2 and Galileo SSI
callisto.artist: NASA / JPL / USGS Astrogeology, Voyager 1 and 2 and Galileo SSI
callisto.usage: The global Galileo and Voyager mosaic supplies the observations. Soft ground and coverage gaps were painted in overlapping equal-area polar views. Separate high-resolution crops restore the southern pole and the equatorial resolution seam and bands. The 8K delivery is scaled to the resolved detail. Parts of Callisto were never photographed or were photographed only at low resolution. Those areas are painted with an image model to continue the photographed ground. The painted details are unobserved.

triton.credit: NASA / JPL-Caltech / Lunar & Planetary Institute, Paul Schenk, from Voyager 2
triton.artist: NASA / JPL-Caltech / Lunar & Planetary Institute, Paul Schenk, from Voyager 2
triton.usage: Paul Schenk’s Voyager 2 mosaic supplies the photographed terrain and color. Reconstructed the unobserved north, replaced the soft south-polar smear using polar coordinates and rebuilt the fine terrain in the blue-green belt, retaining its broad measured color through a wraparound frequency blend. Parts of Triton were never photographed or were photographed only at low resolution. Those areas are painted with an image model to continue the photographed ground. The painted details are unobserved.

charon.credit: NASA / JHUAPL / SwRI / USGS Astrogeology, New Horizons LORRI and MVIC
charon.artist: NASA / JHUAPL / SwRI / USGS Astrogeology, New Horizons LORRI and MVIC
charon.usage: The 300 m New Horizons mosaic supplies the measured relief. The published Char​on color map (https://www.iau.org/public/images/detail/iau1803c/) supplies low-pass chroma for the observed red north polar stain through the previous package texture. The unobserved south and soft margins were painted in overlapping equal-area polar views. A higher-detail south polar crop ties the sharp rim into the newly painted terrain at the 4K delivery scale. Parts of Charon were never photographed or were photographed only at low resolution. Those areas are painted with an image model to continue the photographed ground. The painted details are unobserved.

phobos.credit: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, Phobos Viking Global Mosaic 5m (P. Stooke; DLR control network), from Viking Orbiter images, NASA/JPL. Public domain; the USGS page asks to cite the authors.
phobos.usage: The mosaic's brightness (14400 x 7200, 8-bit), cut to 4096 x 2048 and then to 512, 1024 and 2048 across, longitude 0 in the middle and east to the right, tinted with the body's colour in the package's table and set to the level of its look (scripts/make-moon-maps.py). It is registered with the shape model (Gaskell): the relief of one and the brightness of the other correlate best at no turn.

deimos.credit: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, Deimos Global Mosaic (P. Stooke), from Viking Orbiter images, NASA/JPL. Public domain; the USGS asks to cite the authors.
deimos.usage: The mosaic's brightness, read through the USGS web map service at 2048 x 1024 (the mosaic's native size is not stated), made as Phobos's. Its longitudes are not tied to the shape model by anything the files state: see NOTICE.md.

phoebe.licence: Public domain (NASA/JPL data; NASA's media guidelines, no endorsement implied)
phoebe.credit: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute, Cassini ISS global mosaic of Phoebe (DLR and the Cassini ISS team, 2006; PIA07775 is the same picture). NASA should be acknowledged as the source.
phoebe.artist: DLR and the Cassini ISS team
phoebe.usage: The Cassini ISS mosaic supplies the photographed ground. The white blocks along the south edge and the gap at the north pole are painted to continue that ground. Registered with the shape model (Gaskell) and left unturned, as before. Parts of Phoebe were never photographed or were photographed only at low resolution. Those areas are painted with an image model to continue the photographed ground. The painted details are unobserved.

ariel.credit: NASA / JPL / USGS Astrogeology, Voyager 2 mosaic (Tammy Becker)
ariel.artist: NASA / JPL / USGS Astrogeology, Voyager 2 mosaic (Tammy Becker)
ariel.usage: The USGS Voyager 2 map distributed by JPL supplies the southern observations. The polar repaint fills the unobserved northern hemisphere and reconstructs only fine detail in blurred observed areas. The 4096-pixel output is a texture delivery size. The original optical map is 1440 × 720. Parts of Ariel were never photographed or were photographed only at low resolution. Those areas are painted with an image model to continue the photographed ground. The painted details are unobserved.

miranda.credit: NASA / JPL / USGS Astrogeology, Voyager 2 mosaic (Tammy Becker)
miranda.artist: NASA / JPL / USGS Astrogeology, Voyager 2 mosaic (Tammy Becker)
miranda.usage: The shipped WebP anchors orientation and the released image outside the repair. The Voyager 2 footprint sets an irregular join. Recovered Voyager pixels clipped by the strip where reliable, then matched the adjacent tone and continued the scarps across the old join. Refined three local areas where old vertical smears and soft faceted detail remained, while retaining broad tone and fine detail outside those areas. The photographed southern terrain outside the repair is unchanged from the resampled released texture before WebP encoding. Parts of Miranda were never photographed or were photographed only at low resolution. Those areas are painted with an image model to continue the photographed ground. The painted details are unobserved.
